title: Parents are 90 days from returning to work and still do not know who will take their child
job: Secure workable childcare for a specific start date, age, commute and budget.
trigger: Return-to-work date is fixed but no childcare place is confirmed.
surfaceComplaint: We are on lots of lists, but we have no idea which one will actually turn into a spot.
believedCause: Toronto just needs more daycare spaces.
mechanism: Scarcity is real, but parents also manage independent waitlists, changing vacancies, age transitions, subsidy rules and short response windows. Discovery is only the first step; the pain is ongoing orchestration.

workflow.friction: age, hours, subsidy and commute differ

existingSpend.amount: can be materially above CWELCC fees

economics.painCostNote: Largest cost may be delayed return to work or a much more expensive fallback, not search time itself.

buyer.roiLogic: Small relative to a week of lost work or private-care premium.

intervention.timeToValue: same-day plan; placement may take weeks

experiment.outreach: neighbourhood parent groups and employer ERGs
experiment.success: 6/20 pay and 50% report materially less admin; 4 placements accelerated or made more certain
experiment.kill: parents value listings but will not pay for coordination

claims.text: Toronto childcare operations use formal waitlist procedures and vacancy offers can require response within 48 hours.
The paid wedge should be orchestration rather than another directory.
